definitions.standard: A substance or matter in a state in which it will expand freely to fill the whole of a container, having no fixed shape and no fixed volume.
definitions.simple: A gas is like the air we breathe. It spreads out to fill up whatever space it is inside, like a balloon.
definitions.scientific: A state of matter that has no definite shape or volume. The intermolecular forces are extremely weak, causing particles to move randomly at high speeds.

linguistics.origin: Coined in the 17th century by J.B. van Helmont, from the Greek word 'khaos' (chaos).

advanced_data.history: The study of gases led to the atomic theory of matter.

common_misconceptions: Gases do not have mass. (They do! A balloon full of air weighs more than an empty balloon).
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Use the 'Dance Party' trick: in a gas, everyone is running wildly across the entire room, ignoring each other!
